rows.name: RecallWins
rows.text: Once a drone is recalled, it does not watch again until it has landed.

rows.name: ReturnsWhenIsolated
rows.text: From any situation a drone can be in, it can always get back to landed; an isolated drone included.

rows.name: GeofenceBreachEndsWatch
rows.text: Once a drone is outside its cleared airspace, it does not watch until it has landed.

rows.name: QuarantinedStaysOut
rows.text: Once a drone is quarantined, it takes no part in coordination until it has been readmitted.

rows.name: PositionDriftHazard
rows.text: Without satellite positioning, a drone's position estimate drifts and its reports place objects in the wrong place.

rows.name: MeshJammingHazard
rows.text: Interference cuts the links between drones, and coordination stalls.

rows.name: MisclassificationHazard
rows.text: A detection is reported as the wrong class, or given a forced class where Unknown was the truth.

rows.name: SensingDegradedUnnoticedHazard
rows.text: A sensor degrades and nobody knows the reports from it are unreliable.

rows.name: StaleTrackHazard
rows.text: A track is shown as current after nothing has seen the object for a while.

rows.name: SpoofedMemberHazard
rows.text: Something that is not one of the drones joins the mesh and takes part in coordination.

rows.name: MixedClassifierVersionsHazard
rows.text: Drones run different classifier versions and classify the same object differently.

rows.name: OperatorOverloadHazard
rows.text: More alerts reach the operator than they can judge, and they accept what is in front of them.

rows.name: MemberCollisionHazard
rows.text: two members sharing the same airspace fail to deconflict their flight paths and risk collision.

rows.name: PrematureDepartureHazard
rows.text: a member leaves its sector for recall or recharge before a handover to a peer completes, leaving a gap in watch.

rows.name: UncoveredMemberLossHazard
rows.text: a member is lost or grounded and the fleet does not redistribute coverage quickly enough, leaving its sector unwatched.

rows.name: UnrelayedIsolationHazard
rows.text: an isolated member finds no peer able to relay for it and drops out of coordination without anyone noticing.

rows.name: CoordinationForkHazard
rows.text: under heavy jamming the mesh can partition into two groups; each half, deciding sector handover and redistribution onboard without a ground arbiter, can independently reassign the same sector, and neither half can see the other's claim until the partition heals.

rows.name: GroundBlindSpotHazard
rows.text: because coordination decisions are settled onboard without waiting for ground confirmation, the status picture assembled at the ground station can lag the fleet's true onboard state during a mesh degradation, hiding a genuine coverage gap from the duty controller until the next status update arrives.

rows.name: GroundLinkRadioFailureHazard
rows.text: PA-added: the physical ground link radio on the relaying member, or at the ground station, fails outright rather than merely degrading, losing the ground link regardless of radio interference conditions.

rows.name: RechargeContentionHazard
rows.text: PA-added: more drones need the recharge point at once than the ground crew can turn around within a rotation cycle, so a scheduled handover has no relieving drone.

rows.name: DroneAirVehicleContract
rows.text: Contract a drone air-vehicle HWCI must meet: sortie endurance and on-board compute cost.

rows.name: DroneMissionSoftwareContract
rows.text: Contract the drone mission software CSCI must meet: report holding, no reports lost in a link gap, detection quality, and report latency once the link is up.

rows.name: SafetyMonitorContract
rows.text: Contract the safety-monitor CI must meet: independence from the mission software it can override.

rows.name: MeshRadioContract
rows.text: Contract the mesh radio CI must meet: keep a usable share of peer links available even when half the mesh is jammed.

rows.name: GroundLinkRadioContract
rows.text: Contract the ground-link radio CI must meet: enough independently procured units across the fleet that one radio failing outright does not lose the ground link for good.

rows.name: StoredMapsStoreContract
rows.text: Contract the stored-map store CI must meet: bound a drone's position error after 10 minutes without GNSS.

rows.name: GroundStationContract
rows.text: Contract the ground station hardware CI must meet: enough ground-link port capacity to host the link.

rows.name: GroundControlSoftwareContract
rows.text: Contract the ground control software CI must meet: keep alerts within what the single duty controller can judge, with enough time per alert, and few false alarms.

rows.name: RechargePointContract
rows.text: Contract the recharge point CI must meet: turnaround time per drone and enough simultaneous capacity to avoid recharge contention.

rows.name: CiClassifierAdmissionSkewHazard
rows.text: EPBS hazard: procuring the ground control software CI and the on-board drone mission software CI as independently released configuration items risks the admission gate's registered classifier version drifting out of sync with what a drone is actually running, letting a stale or unregistered classifier version reach the fleet undetected. Distinct from SA::Hazards::MixedClassifierVersionsHazard, which is about the fleet-behaviour effect; this is the CI-release-discipline cause.

rows.name: SafetyMonitorSoleSourceHazard
rows.text: EPBS hazard, accepted: the safety-monitor HWCI is sole-sourced from one supplier line; a disruption or recall of that line would leave the fleet without independently procured override-authority hardware. Accepted per program baseline — managed operationally by contract sparing, outside this model's scope.

rows.name: RechargePointSoleFacilityHazard
rows.text: EPBS hazard, accepted: fielding a single recharge point and ground-crew station is itself a single point of failure for the whole fleet's turnaround, distinct from PA::Hazards::RechargeContentionHazard's bay-scheduling risk — an outage of the facility itself removes charging capability fleet-wide, not just contends for it. Accepted per the program's fixed single-site plan at this fleet size; a redundant site is out of procurement scope.
